title: How It Works - Orbital Temple
heading: How It Works
intro: The Orbital Temple project consists of three interconnected elements that work together to send names to the temple in space.
paragraph1: Once launched, the satellite will orbit Earth at an altitude of approximately 525 km, storing the names in its memory. Ground stations will communicate with the satellite during its passes, transmitting the names that people have submitted through the website.
paragraph2: When you submit a name, it joins a queue. After the satellite reaches orbit, your name will be transmitted during an available pass. You'll receive an email confirmation when your name has been successfully uploaded to the Orbital Temple.
paragraph3: On January 16, 2026, the first satellite was aboard ISRO's PSLV-C62. The rocket reached space but failed to deploy its payload. A backup satellite is ready, and we are working on a new launch.
